author: pgaudet
body: Hi everyone,  We are doing QC on GO-CAM models, and we have found statements that are incorrect with respect to how protein complexes are used:  There are 92 models that have "MF occurs in protein containing complex";  while the correct relation should be gene part of complex, as shown in the example below. This may change the meaning of the annotation, so we prefer that curators review them. The list of annotations is here:  https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1oDhJuY182Rf7ZflctOoRrIPv5r1boyTbis3nQx_eYwo/edit?gid=0#gid=0 group | Number of models  |   -- | -- dictybase |   2 flybase |   3 MGI | 6 uniprot | 10 holthuis-lab-uos.de | 1 pombase |   19 wormbase |   4 xenbase |   2 yeastgenome | 41 zfin |   2 ### Note that there may be more than one instance of the problem in each model. Please let us know if you have any questions. Thanks, Pascale
title: GO-CAM annotation reviews for MF occurs in protein-containing complex

author: ValWood
body:
I can no longer localize entities to the kinetochore because it has "supramolecular complex'
For example the spindle assembly checkpoint is active at the outer kinetochore.
This is also classed as an intracellular anatomical strcuture.
It will be difficult to annotate pathways correctly unless we can use "kinetochore" as a location.

In the ontology, "supramolecular complex" is a direct child of "cellular anatomical anatomical structure".
It is available in the 'occurs in' autocomplete menu.
Does that not work for what you're trying to capture?
